mapper.select: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.dept_name, e.salary FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id JOIN ( SELECT dept_id, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM employee GROUP BY dept_id ) m ON e.dept_id = m.dept_id AND e.salary = m.max_salary ORDER BY d.id

SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.dept_name, e.salary, ROUND(a.avg_salary, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id JOIN ( SELECT dept_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employee GROUP BY dept_id ) a ON e.dept_id = a.dept_id WHERE e.salary > a.avg_salary ORDER BY d.id, e.salary DESC

SELECT d.dept_name, sg.grade, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM salary_grade sg LEFT JOIN employee e ON e.salary BETWEEN sg.low_salary AND sg.high_salary LEFT JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id GROUP BY d.dept_name, sg.grade ORDER BY d.dept_name, sg.grade
SELECT salary FROM employee ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT d.id AS dept_id, d.dept_name, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.dept_name ORDER BY AVG(e.salary) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT name AS employee_name, salary, position FROM employee ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT #{offset}, #{size}
SELECT name AS employee_name, dept_id, hire_date FROM employee ORDER BY hire_date DESC LIMIT #{size}
SELECT e.name AS employee_name, l.name AS leader_name, e.position FROM employee e LEFT JOIN employee l ON e.leader_id = l.id ORDER BY e.id

SELECT e.id AS employee_id, e.name AS employee_name, e.hire_date AS employee_hire_date, d.dept_name, l.name AS leader_name, l.hire_date AS leader_hire_date FROM employee e JOIN employee l ON e.leader_id = l.id JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE e.hire_date < l.hire_date
SELECT d.id AS dept_id, d.dept_name, e.id AS employee_id, e.name AS employee_name, e.salary FROM department d LEFT JOIN employee e ON e.dept_id = d.id ORDER BY d.id, e.id

SELECT d.id AS dept_id, d.dept_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM department d JOIN employee e ON e.dept_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.dept_name HAVING COUNT(e.id) >= #{minCount} ORDER BY employee_count DESC

SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.dept_name, dept_info.cnt AS dept_employee_count FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id JOIN ( SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM employee GROUP BY dept_id ) dept_info ON e.dept_id = dept_info.dept_id WHERE e.position = #{position} ORDER BY d.id, e.id
SELECT e.name AS employee_name, e.salary, d.dept_name FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE d.dept_code = #{deptCode} ORDER BY e.salary DESC

SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.dept_name, l.name AS leader_name, sg.grade AS salary_grade, e.salary FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id LEFT JOIN employee l ON e.leader_id = l.id JOIN salary_grade sg ON e.salary BETWEEN sg.low_salary AND sg.high_salary WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employee) ORDER BY e.salary DESC

SELECT e.name AS employee_name, e.salary, d.dept_name FROM employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE d.id != #{deptId} AND e.salary > ALL ( SELECT salary FROM employee WHERE dept_id = #{deptId} AND salary IS NOT NULL ) ORDER BY e.salary

SELECT d.id AS dept_id, d.dept_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary, ROUND(AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, e.hire_date, CURDATE())), 1) AS avg_service_years FROM department d LEFT JOIN employee e ON e.dept_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.dept_name ORDER BY d.dept_name
SELECT name AS employee_name, salary AS month_salary, salary * 13 AS annual_salary FROM employee ORDER BY annual_salary

SELECT user_id, MIN(login_date) AS start_date, MAX(login_date) AS end_date, COUNT(*) AS continuous_days FROM ( SELECT user_id, login_date, DATE_SUB(login_date, INTERVAL ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date ) DAY) AS grp FROM login_log ) t GROUP BY user_id, grp HAVING COUNT(*) >= #{days} ORDER BY user_id

SELECT category_name, product_name, total_quantity, rn FROM ( SELECT c.name AS category_name, p.name AS product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM product p JOIN category c ON p.category_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_item oi ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, p.id, p.name ) t WHERE rn <= #{topN} ORDER BY category_name, rn

SELECT sale_month, product_name, sale_amount, rn FROM ( SELECT DATE_FORMAT(o.create_time, '%Y-%m') AS sale_month, p.name AS product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) AS sale_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY DATE_FORMAT(o.create_time, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) DESC ) AS rn FROM order_item oi JOIN `orders` o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN product p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY sale_month, p.id, p.name ) t WHERE rn <= #{topN} ORDER BY sale_month DESC, rn

SELECT sg.grade, sg.low_salary, sg.high_salary, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM salary_grade sg LEFT JOIN employee e ON e.salary BETWEEN sg.low_salary AND sg.high_salary GROUP BY sg.grade, sg.low_salary, sg.high_salary ORDER BY sg.grade

SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 0 THEN 1 END) AS pending_payment, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 1 THEN 1 END) AS paid, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 2 THEN 1 END) AS shipped, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 3 THEN 1 END) AS completed, COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 4 THEN 1 END) AS cancelled, COUNT(*) AS total FROM `orders`

SELECT u.username, COALESCE(c.total_amount, 0) AS total_amount, rank() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(c.total_amount, 0) DESC) AS rank_no FROM `user` u LEFT JOIN ( SELECT user_id, SUM(total_amount) AS total_amount FROM `orders` WHERE status IN (1, 2, 3) GROUP BY user_id ) c ON u.id = c.user_id ORDER BY rank_no
